# Verification Evidence

Use this rule before saying a task is complete, fixed, verified, passing, or
ready to ship.

## Evidence Defaults

- Match evidence to the claim being made.
- Prefer the smallest meaningful check that proves the changed behavior.
- Report the exact commands, live checks, screenshots, renders, or manual
  inspections used.
- If a relevant check was skipped, say why.
- If verification is blocked, report the blocker instead of claiming success.
- Do not treat source-level inspection as enough when the user-visible behavior
  depends on a running app, browser, generated artifact, or integration.
- In DDev sessions, keep human-readable claims and proof in `evidence.md` so a
  later turn can see what was verified without replaying the whole chat.

## UI And Runtime Work

For UI, browser, app, or visual work, prefer live evidence when practical:

- local dev server or app launch
- screenshot or rendered output inspection
- responsive/mobile viewport check when relevant
- absence of obvious layout overlap or stale output

## Delivery

Before delivery, summarize evidence in the PR or final handoff. Keep remaining
risks visible instead of hiding them behind a generic "tests passed" sentence.
